reason: Paragraph states verbatim that Sol's reflected light is 'the feminine Luna, who dissolves the king in her moistness'. Direction correct (Luna is the dissolving agent, Rex the dissolved), quote exact, jung-asserts is right since this is Jung's own interpretive statement.

Text: 'the place of matter... is taken by the unconscious, which was projected into it' — the unconscious was projected into matter. Direction correct (subject the-unconscious, projected into object matter). Quote accurate; Jung's own psychological interpretation, so jung-asserts fits.

Text: 'Lion and peacock, emblems of concupiscence and pride, signify the overweening pretensions of the human shadow.' Direction correct (lion is the sign, shadow the signified). Minor compression: the lion (with the peacock) signifies the shadow's overweening pretensions, specifically its concupiscence aspect, not the shadow tout court — acceptable within a 'signifies' edge.

Direction is right but the relation category is wrong. Jung says the uroboros 'is a dramatic symbol for the integration and assimilation of the opposite, i.e., of the shadow' — it SYMBOLIZES shadow-assimilation; it is not itself the agent that assimilates the shadow. An 'assimilates' edge makes a literal agent claim the paragraph does not assert.

correction.subject: ouroboros
correction.note: If the schema needs a plain node object, use relation 'symbolizes-assimilation-of' with object 'the-shadow', or object node 'shadow-integration' if it exists.

reason: Text: 'the first requisite of any thorough psychological method, for consciousness to confront its shadow.' Direction correct (consciousness confronts shadow, not the reverse). Quote exact; Jung's own therapeutic assertion, jung-asserts correct.

'But if the son is the dominant, then Sol is his right eye and Luna his left. The dominant must contain them both' — the filius as dominant contains Sol (right eye). Direction correct. Conditional/normative framing ('if... must') but the containment claim is Jung's own and clearly asserted.
Same sentence as n=6: Luna is the son-dominant's left eye and 'the dominant must contain them both'. Filius-regius contains Luna; direction correct, quote accurate, jung-asserts fits.

'usually the coniunctio precedes the production of the lapis and the latter is understood as the child of Sol and Luna' — reported alchemical designation ('is understood as'), so jung-reports-parallel is exactly the right claim_type. Lapis child-of Sol supported; direction correct.
Same sentence: lapis 'is understood as the child of Sol and Luna'. Child-of Luna supported; reported designation correctly typed as jung-reports-parallel.

'Here Mercurius in feminine form is the queen' — Mercurius appearing in feminine form as the queen supports manifests-as; direction correct. The 'Here' ties it to the text under discussion, but Jung states the identification in his own voice and elaborates it (queen as maternal vessel, medium with the nature of Mercurius), so jung-asserts is acceptable.
'As a matter of fact the queen corresponds to the soul (anima)' — verbatim, Jung's own psychological equation ('as a matter of fact'), direction and claim_type correct.
Same sentence: 'and the king to spirit, the dominant of consciousness.' Rex corresponds-to spirit is Jung's own assertion; direction, quote, claim_type all correct.

'This more exalted attitude raises the status of the anima from that of a temptress to a psychopomp' — the anima becomes psychopomp (from temptress), paralleled by serpent-to-queen in the next sentence. transforms-into is a fair rendering; note the transformation is conditional on the ego renouncing its intentions, but the edge itself is supported.

Quote accurate, but 'enacts' overreaches. Jung says the drama of the alchemist's soul, his individuation process, 'is played out' IN his art and its allegories — the opus is the stage/projection screen for individuation, not the performer of it. The correct relation is symbolic dramatization/projection, not enactment.

correction.subject: the-opus
correction.note: Alternatively 'dramatizes' or 'is-projection-of' if those relations exist; the alchemist's individuation is played out in the opus's allegories.

reason: 'Ruland defines Adam as a synonym for the aqua permanens' — a reported lexicon definition, correctly attributed to Ruland with claim_type jung-quotes-source. Direction and quote accurate.

'Dorn says that the lapis was called "Adam, who bore his invisible Eve hidden in his body"' — quoted designation correctly typed jung-quotes-source with source Dorn; Adam contains (bears hidden in his body) Eve, direction correct. Note the designation is strictly a name of the lapis, but the containment content is exactly what Dorn's phrase asserts of Adam.

Jung writes 'As the transformative substance, therefore, Adam is also the king who is renewed in the bath' — an explicitly qualified symbolic identification within the alchemical role-system (Adam qua arcane/transformative substance takes the king's place in the renewal bath), not a bare identity. A plain 'is' edge overstates it into identity overreach.

correction.subject: adam
correction.note: Qualify: as the transformative substance, Adam is identified with the king renewed in the bath (CW14 §546).

reason: 'The "old dragon" who prepared the bath... is, psychologically, a personification of the instinctual psyche' — ellipsis in quote is faithful (omits only the appositive 'a primeval creature dwelling in the caverns of the earth'). Direction correct; object 'Instinct' matches 'instinctual psyche' closely enough. Jung's own psychological reading, jung-asserts correct.

'It is as though the alchemists were trying to express the fact that the unconscious itself initiates the process of renewal' — Jung asserts this as the fact the symbolism expresses ('the fact that'). Direction correct (unconscious is initiator, renewal the initiated process). Quote accurate.

'the unconscious process by which the self is "reborn" and enters into a state in which it can be experienced. This state is then described as the "filius regius"' — the reborn, experienceable state of the self is what filius regius names. reborn-as captures this; direction correct (self → filius-regius). Quote accurate across the ellipsis.
